units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 5:1:9">Y. Snh. V, 22ᵈ</cite> top <he>משום תּוֹלֵשׁ</he>, v. <cite ref="S02266"><he>קָשַׁשׁ</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 5:1:9">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 15:32">Num. XV, 32</cite>) <he>מלמד שמצאוהו תולש וכ׳</he> the text intimates that they found him tear wood (uproot shrubs) out of the ground; <cite ref="Shabbat 96b">Sabb. 96ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 113">Sifré Num. 113</cite>.
<cite ref="Beitzah 3a:1">Bets. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>גזרה … ויִתְלוֹשׁ</he> we apprehend, lest he may climb up and pluck.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 8:6">B. Kam. VIII, 6</cite> <he>ת׳ בשערו</he> if one plucks his neighbor’s hair.
Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵃ התולש והאורה he who plucks (fruit) or picks (figs); a. fr.—Part. pass. תָּלוּשׁ; f. תְּלוּשָׁה &c. detached, loose, opp. מחובר fixed, immovable.
<cite ref="Chullin 15b:15">Ḥull. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>ת׳ ולבסוף חיברו</he> an object originally loose which one afterwards fixed.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 7:2">B. Mets. VII, 2</cite> <he>העושה … ת׳ מן הקרקע וכ׳</he> the journeyman that works … on what is detached from the ground &c.; a. fr.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 6:4">Yoma VI, 4</cite> <he>היו מְתַלְּשִׁים בשערו</he> they used to pull the hair of the scapegoat; <cite ref="Tosefta Yoma 4:13">Tosef. ib. IV</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Yoma 3:13">III</cite>), 13.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 34">Gen. R. s. 34</cite> <he>ומְתַלְּשִׁין ארזי וכ׳</he> (not <he>מתליש׳</he>) they tore cedars of Lebanon out while walking; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 61:9">Yalk. ib. 61</cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 5:6">Mikv. V, 6</cite> <he>גל שנ׳</he> if a wave was detached (was thrown on the shore, and its connection with the sea severed); <cite ref="Tosefta Mikvaot 4:5">Tosef. ib. IV, 5</cite>. Y. Ḥag. I, 76ᶜ <he>אם … שנִתְלְשׁוּ וכ׳</he> when thou seest Palestinian townships torn away from their places (their inhabitants driven out), know that they failed to maintain teachers &c.; Lam. R. introd. (R. Abba 2) <he>נִתְלָשׁוֹת</he>; a. fr.
